papers.title: SimpleMicrobiome: An integrated web-based platform for streamlined microbiome data analysis and visualization.
papers.abstract: Microbiome studies require multiple analytical steps after initial sequence processing. These steps commonly include data harmonization, preprocessing, taxonomic profiling, diversity analysis, differential abundance testing, predictive modeling, network inference, and preparation of publication-ready outputs. Although robust packages are available for many of these tasks, routine use often depends on command-line workflows, repeated data reformatting, and method-specific scripting. These requirements can limit accessibility for experimental researchers and complicate consistent analysis across
papers.summary: SimpleMicrobiome is a web-based platform that integrates multiple microbiome analysis steps—from data harmonization and taxonomic profiling to diversity analysis, differential abundance testing, predictive modeling, and network inference—into a single user-friendly interface. It aims to make these analyses accessible to experimental researchers without requiring command-line expertise or method-specific scripting.

papers.title: Community-level eDNA decay patterns in marine zooplankton: Implications for optimizing eDNA-based marine environmental monitoring.
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has the potential to greatly transform marine ecological monitoring, yet its capacity for accurate biodiversity estimates is constrained by its decay process. Previous research has largely focused on laboratory-cultured single species, and thus the dynamics of mixed-species eDNA from natural communities remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted a 10-day time-series experiment to track the community-level eDNA decay process following the complete removal of zooplankton, employing an integrated approach of morphological analysis, quantitative PCR (qPCR), metabarcoding
papers.summary: This study tracked how environmental DNA from a natural marine zooplankton community degrades over 10 days after the organisms were removed, using morphology, qPCR, and metabarcoding. It addresses a gap left by prior single-species laboratory decay studies by characterizing mixed-species eDNA decay dynamics. The findings aim to inform how decay processes should be accounted for when using eDNA for marine biodiversity monitoring.

papers.title: Antimicrobial-resistant organism carriage and metagenomic characterization of the microbiome and resistome in veterinary workers.
papers.abstract: Veterinary personnel work in environments with high exposure to antimicrobials and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. However, the extent to which these occupational exposures influence their carriage of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) organisms and the composition of their microbiome and resistome remains poorly understood. The objective of this study was to characterize AMR pathogen carriage and microbiome/resistome composition in veterinary personnel and to assess whether workplace setting and patient-related exposures were associated with detectable differences in these outcomes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) organism carriage and the composition of the microbiome and resistome in veterinary workers, who face high occupational exposure to antimicrobials and resistant pathogens. It examines whether workplace setting and patient-related exposures are associated with detectable differences in AMR carriage and microbiome/resistome profiles.

papers.title: Perseus: Lineage-Aware Refinement of Kraken2 Taxonomic Classification for Long Read Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Long-read metagenomic sequencing improves assembly contiguity and enables genome-resolved analysis of complex microbial communities, but accurate taxonomic classification of long reads and assembled contigs remains challenging. Highly scalable k-mer-based classifiers such as Kraken2 frequently over-assign fine-rank taxonomic labels when applied to long-read data, producing high false positive classification rates driven by sparse or localized k-mer matches, particularly in microbiomes with extensive taxonomic novelty.
papers.summary: Perseus is a new method that refines Kraken2 taxonomic classifications for long-read metagenomes by using lineage-aware information to correct over-assignment of fine-rank labels. It addresses the high false-positive rates that occur when k-mer-based classifiers are applied to long reads, especially in microbiomes with extensive taxonomic novelty.

papers.title: Symbiotic interactions and climate change implications of the octocoral microbiome.
papers.abstract: Octocorals are vital components of tropical, temperate, and cold-water benthic marine ecosystems. Their associated microbiomes, comprising microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses, are increasingly recognised as central to host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defence. Metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have uncovered taxonomic and functional complexity within these microbial communities, revealing patterns of host specificity and health status, along with seasonality and geographic structuring. However, anthropogenic stressors, particularly those associated with global climate change
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on octocoral microbiomes, which include microeukaryotes, prokaryotes, and viruses, and their roles in host health, nutrient cycling, and chemical defense. It highlights how metagenomics and amplicon sequencing have revealed host specificity, seasonal and geographic patterns, and how climate change stressors threaten these symbiotic relationships.

papers.title: The canine gut microbiome as a translational model for human health and aging.
papers.abstract: The domestic dog is increasingly recognized as a complementary translational model for microbiome research relevant to human health while also offering direct benefits for veterinary medicine. Dogs share environments and dietary exposures with humans and show substantial taxonomic and gene-content similarity to the human gut microbiome, although the apparent degree of similarity depends strongly on whether read recruitment, gene-catalog overlap, or functional overlap is assessed. Dogs also develop spontaneous chronic enteropathies, obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, cancers, cognitive d
papers.summary: This review argues that the domestic dog is a valuable translational model for studying the gut microbiome's role in human health and aging, given shared environments, diets, and substantial taxonomic and functional similarity to the human gut microbiome. It notes that the apparent degree of similarity depends on the analytical approach used (read recruitment, gene-catalog overlap, or functional overlap), and highlights that dogs naturally develop chronic enteropathies, obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, cancers, and cognitive decline relevant to human conditions.

papers.title: Molecular mimicry and functional convergence of bacterial proteins in host-microbe interactions.
papers.abstract: Bacterial proteins modulate host immunity through diverse molecular strategies that are often broadly described as molecular mimicry. However, inconsistent terminology has obscured distinctions between genuine host-like interactions and other forms of host-directed immune modulation. We propose an operational framework that classifies bacterial proteins into four mechanistic categories: molecular mimicry, mimic-like behavior, functional convergence, and pathway interference. The framework prioritizes explicit criteria, including host-target engagement, interaction-interface similarity, functio
papers.summary: This perspective proposes a four-category operational framework to clarify how bacterial proteins modulate host immunity, distinguishing true molecular mimicry from mimic-like behavior, functional convergence, and pathway interference. By prioritizing explicit criteria such as host-target engagement and interaction-interface similarity, it aims to resolve terminological inconsistencies that have blurred mechanistic distinctions in host-microbe interaction research.

papers.title: RAPID: an interactive R/Shiny platform for end-to-end 16S rRNA and ITS amplicon sequence analysis using DADA2.
papers.abstract: Amplicon sequencing of 16S rRNA and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) gene regions is the most widely used approach for characterizing bacterial and fungal communities. The DADA2 pipeline has become the standard for inferring amplicon sequence variants (ASVs), offering single-nucleotide resolution over traditional OTU clustering. However, executing the full DADA2 workflow requires R programming proficiency and manual coordination of multiple sequential steps, presenting a substantial barrier for researchers in clinical, environmental, and agricultural sciences who lack computational training.
papers.summary: RAPID is an interactive R/Shiny platform that wraps the DADA2 amplicon sequencing pipeline into a graphical interface for end-to-end 16S rRNA and ITS analysis. It removes the need for R programming skills and manual step coordination, making ASV-based microbiome analysis accessible to non-computational researchers in clinical, environmental, and agricultural fields.

papers.title: Multi-omics evidence reveals robust airborne-human resistome connectivity driven by high-risk ARGs and mediated by Staphylococcus.
papers.abstract: Airborne microbiomes are considered an important source of human antimicrobial resistance (AMR) exposure, yet multi-omics evidence linking airborne and human nasal resistomes remains limited. Here, we integrated metagenomic sequencing and whole-genome sequencing of antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus isolates to investigate the connectivity between air and human nasal resistomes in dairy farm environments. Metagenomic taxonomic profiling showed that Staphylococcus was prominent in total suspended particles (TSP) and consistently detected across all samples. Among environmental reservoirs, TSP
papers.summary: This study integrates metagenomics and whole-genome sequencing of antibiotic-resistant Staphylococcus isolates to show that airborne resistomes in dairy farm environments are strongly connected to human nasal resistomes. Staphylococcus appears to act as a key mediator carrying high-risk antibiotic resistance genes between air and humans, suggesting airborne transmission is an important route of AMR exposure.

papers.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Taxonomic profiling is fundamental to microbiome research, yet achieving high species-level accuracy remains challenging for complex communities that span bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea, and these limitations are exacerbated in low-biomass, host-dominated samples. We introduce Metax, a cross-domain taxonomic profiler that integrates coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to distinguish true microbial signals from artifacts. Across >600 samples from host-associated, environmental, wastewater, and low-biomass clinical settings, including benc
papers.summary: Metax is a new cross-domain taxonomic profiler for metagenomes that combines coverage-based probabilistic modeling with an expectation-maximization framework to improve species-level accuracy across bacteria, viruses, eukaryotes, and archaea. It was validated on over 600 samples from diverse environments, including low-biomass and host-dominated clinical samples where existing tools struggle.

papers.title: Landscape of retron diversity across the SPIRE microbial metagenome resource reveals candidate novel type XI-like lineages.
papers.abstract: Retrons are bacterial genetic elements encoding a specialized reverse transcriptase (RT) that synthesizes multicopy single-stranded DNA and are increasingly recognized as components of bacterial anti-phage defense systems. However, their diversity and ecological distribution across large-scale genomic resources remain poorly characterized. Here, we surveyed retron RTs across the SPIRE representative metagenome collection, a non-redundant, species-level data set spanning diverse microbial habitats. Using a curated panel of type-specific hidden Markov models, we identified retrons representing a
papers.summary: This study surveyed retron reverse transcriptases across the SPIRE metagenome collection, a large non-redundant species-level resource spanning diverse microbial habitats. Using type-specific hidden Markov models, the authors uncovered substantial retron diversity and identified candidate novel type XI-like lineages. The work expands knowledge of these bacterial anti-phage defense elements and their ecological distribution.

papers.title: Phylogenomics of Desulfuromonadia supports reclassification of Geobacter psychrophilus as Irobacter psychrophilus comb. nov. and proposal of Geosyntrophus gen. nov.
papers.abstract: Genome-resolved phylogenomics reveals widespread misclassification of metal-reducing bacteria historically assigned to Geobacter based on 16S rRNA gene phylogeny, and highlights species that persist only as 16S rRNA entries without genomes for robust taxonomic resolution. Here, we resolve two such lineages by integrating whole-genome phylogeny with average amino acid identity (AAI) and percentage of conserved proteins (POCP) across 418 dereplicated genomes of Desulfuromonadia. We report a draft genome of the psychrophilic iron-reducing bacterium Geobacter psychrophilus (100% completeness). Phy
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved phylogenomics across 418 Desulfuromonadia genomes to show that many metal-reducing bacteria historically classified as Geobacter based on 16S rRNA are misclassified. The authors reclassify Geobacter psychrophilus as Irobacter psychrophilus comb. nov. and propose the new genus Geosyntrophus, integrating whole-genome phylogeny with AAI and POCP metrics.

papers.title: Wastewater-derived gut microbiome: global patterns and associations with population health.
papers.abstract: Urban wastewater systems aggregate gut microbiome signals from large populations, enabling exploration of their associations with population-level health patterns. However, it remains unclear whether wastewater-derived gut microbiome (WGM) simply represents a composite of individual gut microbes or whether it forms structured ecological patterns with potential relevance to population-level health-burden gradients. We analyzed 661 untreated wastewater metagenomes from 220 cities across 97 countries spanning all inhabited continents to characterize the global WGM. WGM exhibited broad phylogeneti
papers.summary: This study analyzed 661 untreated wastewater metagenomes from 220 cities across 97 countries to characterize global patterns in the wastewater-derived gut microbiome (WGM). The authors found that WGM exhibits structured ecological patterns rather than simply reflecting a composite of individual gut microbes, and these patterns show associations with population-level health burdens. The work suggests wastewater surveillance could serve as a scalable tool for monitoring population health gradients globally.

papers.title: Genome-resolved analysis reveals disruption of gut microbial vitamin B and K2 biosynthesis during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii infection remodels the gut microbiome, yet its impact on microbial vitamin biosynthetic potential and host redox metabolism remains unclear. Here, we integrated mouse gut metagenomes with publicly available metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) to construct a genome-resolved atlas of B-vitamin and vitamin K2 biosynthesis. From 45,697 MAGs, we curated 4,771 representative genomes, of which 2,682 met high-quality criteria (completeness ≥90%, contamination <5%). Functional annotation identified 229,717 vitamin-related genes corresponding to 177 Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Geno
papers.summary: This study used genome-resolved metagenomics to map the biosynthetic potential for B vitamins and vitamin K2 in the mouse gut microbiome during Toxoplasma gondii infection. By curating thousands of metagenome-assembled genomes, the authors found that infection disrupts microbial vitamin biosynthesis pathways, which may contribute to altered host redox metabolism. The work links a parasitic infection to functional shifts in the gut microbiome's vitamin-producing capacity.

papers.title: Performance Profiles of Short DNA Barcode Segments for Family Level Detection of Asteraceae Within Asterales.
papers.abstract: Short DNA barcodes may facilitate sequence recovery from degraded material, but their ability to retain target-family identity while excluding related taxa varies among genomic regions. We computationally evaluated 16 nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial marker regions from 11 Asterales families using 279,956 NCBI locus-record matches and an accession-disjoint discovery/test design. Thirty-one candidate segments of 50-200 bp (mean, 98.55 bp) were screened in discovery data and evaluated for within-Asteraceae sequence recall, differentiation from non-Asteraceae Asterales, in silico primer behavi
papers.summary: This study computationally evaluated 16 nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial marker regions to identify short DNA barcode segments (50-200 bp) that can reliably identify the plant family Asteraceae while excluding related families within Asterales. Using nearly 280,000 NCBI locus records with a discovery/test split, they screened 31 candidate segments for within-family recall, differentiation from non-Asteraceae taxa, and primer feasibility. The work provides a systematic performance profile of short barcodes for family-level detection, useful for degraded or low-quality plant material.

papers.title: Physiological Mechanisms of Silicon-Induced Drought Tolerance in Crops.
papers.abstract: Drought is one of the most damaging abiotic stresses affecting global crop productivity, and its frequency and severity are projected to increase under ongoing climate change. Silicon (Si), although not classified as an essential nutrient, is increasingly regarded as a "quasi-essential" beneficial element that improves crop performance under water-limited conditions. This review summarises the physiological mechanisms of Si-induced drought tolerance, based mainly on literature published in the past five years. Rather than presenting these mechanisms as an inventory of separate physiological ef
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent literature on how silicon, though not an essential nutrient, helps crops tolerate drought. It describes the physiological mechanisms—such as improved water retention, antioxidant defense, and osmotic adjustment—through which silicon mitigates drought stress, framing them as interconnected rather than isolated effects.

papers.title: Large-scale benchmarking of prokaryotic annotation tools across thousands of species.
papers.abstract: Genome annotation is an important step in deriving functional meaning from prokaryotic sequencing data, yet systematic evaluations guiding tool selection are lacking. We present the first large-scale investigation of four prominent open-source annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes. This includes Escherichia coli strains for baseline performance, thousands of archaea and bacteria genomes, as well as frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.summary: This study benchmarks four widely used prokaryotic genome annotation tools (Prokka, Bakta, EggNOG-mapper, and PGAP) across 156,033 diverse genomes, including E. coli, archaea, bacteria, and challenging inputs like frameshifted and metagenome-assembled genomes. It provides the first large-scale systematic comparison to guide tool selection for functional annotation of prokaryotic sequencing data.

papers.title: Targeting Stress and the Gut-Brain Axis: Effects of Lifestyle and Psychobiotic Interventions on the Gut Microbiome in Adults-A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Stress is increasingly recognized as an important modulator of gut microbiome composition and function through the bidirectional microbiota-gut-brain axis. Dietary, psychobiotic, and other lifestyle-oriented interventions have therefore attracted growing interest as potential strategies for simultaneously influencing stress-related outcomes and the gut microbiome. This systematic review aimed to evaluate randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating the effects of lifestyle-oriented and psychobiotic interventions on both stress-related outcomes and the gut microbiome
papers.summary: This systematic review examines randomized controlled trials testing whether lifestyle and psychobiotic interventions can simultaneously improve stress-related outcomes and alter gut microbiome composition in adults. It synthesizes evidence on the microbiota-gut-brain axis as a target for dietary and behavioral interventions.

papers.title: Spatially Specialized Nasopharynx-Rectal Microbiomes in Golden Snub-Nosed Monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana).
papers.abstract: Understanding the nasopharyngeal (NAS) and rectal (INT) microbiomes is critical to maintain host health. However, their functional roles in shaping microbial network structure and niche differentiation remain unexplored in most animal species, especially endangered primates. Here, we compared the NAS and INT microbiomes of golden snub-nosed monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana) using full-length 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and metagenomics, focusing on taxonomic composition, functional profiles (KEGG, CAZy, PHI), and microbial co-occurrence networks.
papers.summary: This study compares the nasopharyngeal and rectal microbiomes of endangered golden snub-nosed monkeys using full-length 16S rRNA sequencing and metagenomics. It characterizes taxonomic composition, functional profiles (KEGG, CAZy, PHI), and microbial co-occurrence networks, revealing site-specific microbial communities and niche differentiation between the two body sites.

papers.title: Effects of Dietary Glucose, Fructose, and Monosaccharide-to-Lard Energy Ratios on Cecal Microbiota Composition and Ecological Organization in Rats.
papers.abstract: Background: Although dietary fat and carbohydrates are major determinants of gut microbiota composition, their interactive effects across changing dietary monosaccharide-to-lard energy ratios remain incompletely understood. This study descriptively examined treatment-level cecal microbiome profiles across dietary gradients in which lard (L) was progressively replaced with glucose (G) or fructose (F). Methods: A carbohydrate-free, lard-rich control diet was formulated, and lard was progressively replaced with glucose or fructose while maintaining a constant protein-to-energy ratio. Cecal conten
papers.summary: This study examined how progressively replacing dietary lard with glucose or fructose affects cecal microbiota composition and ecological organization in rats. The authors found that the type of monosaccharide and the monosaccharide-to-fat energy ratio both shape microbiome structure, with glucose and fructose producing distinct microbial community profiles. The work highlights that dietary fat-carbohydrate interactions, not just individual nutrients, influence gut microbial ecology.

papers.title: Phage bioinformatics tools: a review of computational approaches for bacteriophage research.
papers.abstract: Rising clinical interest in phage therapy and the exponential growth of metagenomic sequence catalogues have driven a rapid expansion of bacteriophage bioinformatics. More than 80 dedicated tools, mostly published since 2020, now span identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. Aimed at experienced practitioners and developers, this review synthesizes the field through the lens of three successive computational paradigms: sequence homology, bounded by database completeness; machine learning, constrained by labelled traini
papers.summary: This review surveys over 80 computational tools for bacteriophage research, most published since 2020, covering tasks such as phage identification, assembly, annotation, taxonomy, lifestyle prediction, defence-system detection, and host prediction. It organizes the field around three successive paradigms—sequence homology, machine learning, and (implied) newer approaches—and discusses the limitations each faces, such as database completeness and labelled training data.

papers.title: Foundation Models for Microbiome Research: From Sequence Semantics to Community Dynamics and Multimodal World Models.
papers.abstract: Microbiome sequencing has advanced faster than microbiome understanding. Although large-scale 16S, metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and proteomic datasets have accumulated rapidly, most analyses remain cohort-specific and association-driven, limiting mechanistic insight, cross-study transferability, and robustness to technical confounding. Foundation models offer a new computational framework by learning reusable biological representations from large unlabeled datasets. In this Review, we present microbiome foundation models as a hierarchy spanning biological scales. Sequence-centric models ca
papers.summary: This review argues that foundation models—large pretrained neural networks learning reusable representations from unlabeled data—can unify microbiome research across biological scales, from sequence-level semantics to community dynamics and multimodal integration. It proposes a hierarchy of microbiome foundation models and frames them as a path beyond cohort-specific, association-driven analyses toward more transferable and mechanistically grounded insights.

papers.title: Identifying fundamental gaps in functional metagenomics: a step towards unlocking microbiome research potential.
papers.abstract: Incomplete functional annotation limits biological interpretation in microbiome studies and their translational potential. Poor annotation arises from multiple causes, with incomplete gene-protein-reaction mapping being one tractable yet under-examined contributor. We address this gap by developing a comprehensive hierarchical framework that systematically integrates gene families in UniRef, proteins in UniProt, and metabolic reactions in MetaCyc and BioCyc through UniProtKB accession, EC number, and Pfam-domain matching. Applied to a human gut metagenome dataset via HUMAnN3, our MetaCyc-based
papers.summary: The authors developed a hierarchical framework that links gene families (UniRef), proteins (UniProt), and metabolic reactions (MetaCyc/BioCyc) via UniProtKB accessions, EC numbers, and Pfam domains to improve functional annotation in metagenomics. Applying it to a human gut metagenome with HUMAnN3, they identify gaps in gene-protein-reaction mapping that limit biological interpretation of microbiome data. The work highlights a tractable route to improving functional annotation and unlocking translational potential in microbiome research.

papers.title: Lifestyle Impacts the Oral Microbiome of Classical and Post-Classical Societies in Italy.
papers.abstract: The fall of the Roman Empire (476 CE) profoundly affected the lives of its peoples due to the political, administrative, and territorial changes that occurred. The majority of written records of the time focus on the social élite, leaving larger parts of the population understudied. Here, we employ a bioarchaeological approach to understand how differences in lifestyle may be reflected in the oral microbiome of people from different social classes living before and after the fall.
papers.summary: This study uses bioarchaeological analysis of dental calculus to reconstruct oral microbiomes from individuals of different social classes living before and after the fall of the Roman Empire in Italy. The authors test whether lifestyle differences tied to social status and the political upheaval of 476 CE are reflected in oral microbial communities. The work highlights how ancient microbiomes can serve as a proxy for reconstructing past lifeways often missing from historical records.

papers.title: Assembly Dynamics and Functional Divergence of Anaerobic Communities Driven by Iron Oxides.
papers.abstract: Iron oxides play an important role in regulating global biogeochemical cycles, yet how their physicochemical properties influence community structure, function, and assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of four representative iron oxides-ferrihydrite (Fh), goethite (Gt), haematite (Ht), and magnetite (Mt)-serving as terminal electron acceptors on microbial communities enriched from activated sludge. Metagenomic profiling revealed mineral-dependent divergence in community composition and functional potential. The communities developed on amorphous Fh demonstrated
papers.summary: This study shows that different iron oxide minerals (ferrihydrite, goethite, haematite, magnetite) acting as terminal electron acceptors drive distinct microbial community compositions and functional potentials in anaerobic enrichments from activated sludge. Amorphous ferrihydrite supported notably different communities than the more crystalline minerals, indicating that mineral physicochemical properties shape community assembly and function.

papers.title: The Gut Microbiota in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Evaluation of Microbial Profiles, Disease Activity, Biomarkers, and Treatment Response.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with complex etiopathogenesis, and variable clinical course. The human gastrointestinal (GI) tract is a dynamic ecosystem in which micro-organisms influence metabolism, immune signalling, and pathogen resistance. Understanding these interactions is key to exploring the microbiota's role in RA. This review examines how intestinal and oral microbiota differ in RA patients and influence disease activity and treatment response.
papers.summary: This review examines how the composition of gut and oral microbiota differs in rheumatoid arthritis patients compared to healthy individuals, and how these microbial differences relate to disease activity, biomarkers, and response to treatment. It synthesizes current evidence on the microbiota's role in RA pathogenesis and its potential as a therapeutic or predictive target.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Multidimensional Phenotyping of Gut Metabolic States for Personalized Prebiotic, Probiotic, and Postbiotic Strategies.
papers.abstract: This study presents multidimensional physicochemical phenotyping of human gut metabolic states using integrated multimodal profiling and machine learning. A total of 680 stool samples were analyzed using time-resolved optical, electrochemical, acoustic, magnetic, and spectral measurements implemented in a compact 3D-printed screening platform. Multivariate analysis explained 78.4% of structured variance, and cluster optimization identified seven primary clusters and 26 structurally retained subclusters representing proteolytic, saccharolytic, bile/lipid-rich, oxidative, diarrheal, pigment-link
papers.summary: This study used a compact 3D-printed platform to collect optical, electrochemical, acoustic, magnetic, and spectral measurements from 680 stool samples, then applied machine learning to identify distinct gut metabolic states. The analysis revealed seven primary clusters and 26 subclusters, such as proteolytic, saccharolytic, and bile/lipid-rich states, which could guide personalized prebiotic, probiotic, and postbiotic strategies.

papers.title: Inclusion of Multi-Omic Biomarkers Improves Prediction Accuracy of Response, Relapse, and Overall Survival in Acute Myeloid Leukemia Patients Receiving High-Intensity Induction Chemotherapy.
papers.abstract: Despite advancements in genetic markers for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) risk stratification, outcome prediction remains challenging due to disease heterogeneity and dynamic genetic changes, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers to improve AML treatment strategies and patient outcomes. To refine outcome predictions, we investigated the use of microbial-derived biomarkers to predict composite complete remission (CRc), relapse, and survival for patients on high- and low-intensity regimens, and to integrate those variables into the widely clinically utilized European Leukemia Network (ELN
papers.summary: This study investigated whether adding microbial-derived biomarkers to standard genetic markers improves prediction of complete remission, relapse, and overall survival in acute myeloid leukemia patients undergoing high-intensity induction chemotherapy. The authors found that incorporating multi-omic (including microbiome-derived) features alongside the European Leukemia Network risk classification enhanced predictive accuracy for these clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Evaluating the probiotic potential of Bacillus pumilus HFS2 isolated from the gut microbiota of Heteropneustes fossilis for aquaculture applications.
papers.abstract: Probiotics are increasingly used in aquaculture to enhance fish survival, growth, and health, offering a sustainable approach to fish farming.
papers.summary: This study isolated Bacillus pumilus HFS2 from the gut microbiota of the freshwater catfish Heteropneustes fossilis and evaluated its potential as a probiotic for aquaculture. The authors characterize the strain's beneficial properties, suggesting it could serve as a sustainable feed additive to improve fish survival, growth, and health.

papers.title: Integrated immunoinformatics for the design of novel multi-epitope vaccine and identification of new drug targets against Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, a multidrug-resistant superbug.
papers.abstract: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia is a multidrug-resistant opportunistic pathogen causing severe hospital-acquired infections, especially in immunocompromised patients. The absence of an effective vaccine and rising antibiotic resistance underscore the need for novel interventions. This study employed an integrated reverse vaccinology and computational analyses to identify new immunogenic targets, design a multi-epitope vaccine (MEV), and propose potential drug targets.
papers.summary: This study uses reverse vaccinology and computational immunoinformatics to identify immunogenic protein targets in the multidrug-resistant pathogen Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. The authors design a multi-epitope vaccine construct and propose new drug targets as alternatives to failing antibiotics. The work is entirely computational, so experimental validation of the vaccine and targets remains to be done.

papers.title: In silico genome mining and characterization of putative horse feces-derived bacterial phytases as potential monogastric animal feed additive candidates.
papers.abstract: Phytic acid exerts a significant antinutritional effect in poultry, swine, and fish, which can be mitigated by supplementing monogastric feeds with efficient microbial phytases. Accordingly, mining bacterial genomes for novel phytases represents a strategic computational approach to identifying candidates for improving monogastric animal nutrition. In this study, 162 bacterial genomes associated with horse feces were systematically mined using an in silico pipeline to identify and characterize putative phytases.A total of 69 non-redundant sequences were identified and classified as histidine a
papers.summary: This study used computational genome mining to identify putative phytase enzymes from 162 bacterial genomes associated with horse feces, yielding 69 non-redundant candidate sequences. These phytases are proposed as potential feed additives to improve phosphorus availability in monogastric animals like poultry and swine by breaking down antinutritional phytic acid.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into pathogen diversity and public health risk of Haemaphysalis longicornis in Gansu Province of China.
papers.abstract: The tick Haemaphysalis longicornis vectors numerous zoonotic pathogens, yet its pathogen diversity and associated spatial health risks are not fully characterized. To profile this vector, we performed metagenomic sequencing on 290 H. longicornis ticks across 29 sites in Gansu Province, China. We resolved 25 bacterial and one protozoan genera, with computational analyses revealing population-level distribution patterns and identifying environmental factors as key drivers of spatial variation.We detected marker genes associated with 12 pathogenic microorganisms. Alongside established threats (Ri
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of 290 Haemaphysalis longicornis ticks from 29 sites in Gansu Province, China, to profile the pathogens they carry. The authors identified 25 bacterial and one protozoan genera, including marker genes for 12 pathogenic microorganisms, and found that environmental factors drive spatial variation in pathogen distribution. The work maps tick-borne pathogen diversity and highlights public health risks in this region.

papers.title: Distinctive Patterns of Gut Bifidobacterium Diversity in Mongolian Adults: Regional Variation and Dairy Intake Associations.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Despite increasing interest in the human gut microbiome, particularly in Bifidobacterium, studies focusing on traditionally living populations with high habitual dairy consumption remain limited. This study investigated species-level diversity, abundance, and regional variation of Bifidobacterium among healthy Mongolian adults and contextualized these findings within a global comparative framework. Methods: A total of 100 healthy adults were recruited from four Mongolian regions. Fecal samples were analyzed using species-resolved shotgun metagenomics, and dietary intake
papers.summary: This study used species-resolved shotgun metagenomics to profile gut Bifidobacterium diversity in 100 healthy Mongolian adults across four regions, finding distinctive patterns linked to regional variation and habitual dairy consumption. The findings are contextualized within a global comparative framework, highlighting how traditional diets shape microbiome composition.

papers.title: Dataset characterising dominant bacterial phylotypes across animal manure-enriched composting microcosms for crude oil waste sludge bioremediation.
papers.abstract: The dataset provides a complete record of microbial, functional, physicochemical, and contaminant dynamics from controlled co-composting microcosms designed to remediate petroleum refinery sludge using targeted animal manure amendments. Five treatments-cow, pig, horse, and poultry manures, as well as an unamended control-were monitored over 300 days. The study incorporated amplicon-based 16S rRNA gene sequencing, functional gene inference, culture-based validation, bulk chemistry, and chromatographic analyses. Illumina MiSeq profiling of the V1-V3 regions identified 359 bacterial genera (raw O
papers.summary: This Data in Brief article describes a 300-day co-composting experiment that tracked bacterial communities, functional genes, chemistry, and contaminant levels across five manure-amended treatments (cow, pig, horse, poultry, and unamended control) used to bioremediate petroleum refinery sludge. The dataset includes 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing (V1-V3, Illumina MiSeq) identifying 359 bacterial genera, plus culture-based validation and chromatographic analyses. It provides a reusable resource for researchers studying manure-driven microbial dynamics in hydrocarbon-contaminated waste remediation.

papers.title: Gut microbiome-metabolome signatures of osteosarcopenia in fracture patients in China.
papers.abstract: Osteosarcopenia, defined as the coexistence of low bone mass and sarcopenia, is a disabling musculoskeletal condition, yet its gut microbial and metabolic characteristics in clinical populations remain incompletely understood. Integrative multi-omics approaches may help clarify species-metabolite networks associated with this condition, particularly in fracture patients.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics to characterize gut microbiome and metabolome signatures in Chinese fracture patients with osteosarcopenia, a condition combining low bone mass and muscle loss. It aims to identify species-metabolite networks associated with the disease, addressing a gap in clinical understanding of the gut-muscle-bone axis.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of the fecal microbiome in Lamp2 knockout mice reveals limited genotype-associated differences under standard housing.
papers.abstract: Lysosomal pathways influence host-microbe interactions, but the microbiome consequences of lysosomal dysfunction remain incompletely defined. LAMP2 is required for autophagosome-lysosome fusion, and pathogenic variants in LAMP2 cause Danon disease. Whether Lamp2 loss alters the gut microbiome in vivo has not been systematically evaluated using methods that profile both taxonomic composition and microbial functional potential, such as shotgun metagenomics.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the fecal microbiome of Lamp2 knockout mice, a model for Danon disease, compared to wild-type mice under standard housing conditions. Despite the known role of lysosomal dysfunction in host-microbe interactions, the authors found only limited taxonomic and functional differences associated with the Lamp2 genotype. The results suggest that Lamp2 loss alone does not substantially reshape the gut microbiome in this controlled setting.

papers.title: Genome-resolved gut metagenomics identifies an Escherichia coli-Collinsella signature associated with Wagner 4 gangrenous diabetic foot ulcers.
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are a major complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus, but whether the gut microbiome captures systemic microbial features associated with advanced ulcer severity remains unclear. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 43 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and active DFU, comparing Wagner grades 1-3 (n = 30) with Wagner 4 gangrenous disease (n = 13). De novo assembly and binning recovered 440 dereplicated metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) meeting medium-quality or high-completeness/low-contamination thresholds. Community-level diversit
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from 43 type 2 diabetes patients with diabetic foot ulcers to compare gut microbiome profiles between Wagner grades 1-3 and Wagner 4 gangrenous disease. They recovered 440 metagenome-assembled genomes and identified an Escherichia coli-Collinsella signature associated with the more severe gangrenous ulcers. The findings suggest that gut microbiome composition may reflect or contribute to systemic features linked to DFU severity.

papers.title: A metagenomic analysis of the gut microbiota in a mouse model of fish allergy.
papers.abstract: Fish are among the most frequent causes of immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated food allergies (Type I). Currently, there is no known cure for fish allergy and individuals who are sensitized have to practice strict, lifelong avoidance of fish products in their diets. The relationship between gut microbiome and food allergies is currently a major topic of discussion; these pathologies involve the development of dysbiosis, which is a microbial imbalance resulting from immune-related mechanisms. Recent studies have provided evidence that individuals suffering from food allergies, display an intestinal
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize gut microbiota composition in a mouse model of fish allergy, aiming to identify microbial taxa or functional shifts associated with IgE-mediated sensitization. The work contributes to the broader effort to link food allergy pathology with gut dysbiosis, though the abstract is truncated and specific findings are not detailed.

papers.title: Beyond the Pancreas: The Gut Microbiota in Acute Pancreatitis - From Mechanisms to Therapeutic Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Acute pancreatitis is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease in which severe forms are frequently complicated by intestinal barrier failure, dysbiosis, bacterial translocation, infected necrosis, systemic inflammation, and organ dysfunction. Growing clinical and experimental evidence suggests that the gut microbiota may contribute to disease progression and represents a potential, although incompletely validated, therapeutic target. Importantly, acute pancreatitis-associated dysbiosis involves not only taxonomic shifts but also functional metabolic reprogramming, including reduced short-chain fa
papers.summary: This review examines how gut microbiota changes contribute to acute pancreatitis progression, focusing on mechanisms like intestinal barrier failure, dysbiosis, bacterial translocation, and infected necrosis. It highlights that dysbiosis involves not just taxonomic shifts but also functional metabolic reprogramming, such as reduced short-chain fatty acid production, positioning the microbiota as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: The chromosomal genome sequence of a staghorn coral, Acropora cf.  manni (Scleractinia: Acroporidae).
papers.abstract: We present a genome assembly from a colony sample of Acropora cf. manni (staghorn coral; Cnidaria; Anthozoa; Scleractinia; Acroporidae). The assembly contains two haplotypes with total lengths of 459.26 megabases and 489.30 megabases. Most of haplotype 1 (94.39%) is scaffolded into 14 chromosomal pseudomolecules. Haplotype 2 was assembled to scaffold level. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled, with a length of 18.48 kilobases. Metagenome binning recovered one bacterial bin from the phylum Chlamydiota.
papers.summary: This paper reports a chromosomal-level genome assembly for a staghorn coral, Acropora cf. manni, with two haplotypes of roughly 459 and 489 megabases, most of haplotype 1 scaffolded into 14 chromosomes. The mitochondrial genome was also assembled, and a bacterial symbiont genome from the phylum Chlamydiota was recovered via metagenome binning. This provides a new genomic resource for coral biology and reef conservation research.

papers.title: Gut microbiota dynamics and metabolic pathways associated with bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis progression.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive respiratory disease characterized by epithelial injury, aberrant repair and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. Although the gut-lung axis is increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders, stage-resolved characterization of gut microbiota taxonomic and functional potential during PF development is limited.
papers.summary: This study characterizes how gut microbiota composition and predicted metabolic functions change across stages of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis in a mouse model. It provides stage-resolved taxonomic and functional profiles that link gut microbial dynamics to fibrosis progression via the gut-lung axis.

papers.title: Short-read genome skimming enables molecular barcoding of old myxomycete collections.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of Illumina-based genome skimming for barcoding myxomycete herbarium collections ranging from 29 to 91 years in age. We successfully retrieved partial sequences of the standard marker gene (nucSSU) in all cases, as well as additional markers (mtSSU, EF1a, and COI) for certain collections. Altogether, 28 genes were recognized in the studied material. In a 33-year-old specimen of Lindbladia tubulina, the assembly reached an N50 of 4.19 kb, enabling the recovery of extended functional loci. The input genomic DNA quantity emerges as the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study shows that Illumina genome skimming can successfully recover barcode sequences from myxomycete herbarium specimens up to 91 years old, retrieving the standard nucSSU marker in all samples and additional markers in some. The amount of input genomic DNA was the main factor determining success, and one 33-year-old specimen yielded an assembly with an N50 of 4.19 kb, allowing recovery of extended functional loci.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors in sediments of river Yamuna.
papers.abstract: Riverine sediments serve as critical reservoirs of microbial diversity and functional genes, reflecting both natural ecological processes and anthropogenic impacts. In the present study, we employed a shotgun metagenomic approach to investigate microbial community composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes, and virulence factors in sediments collected from three environmentally distinct locations of the Yamuna River near Agra, India, representing BSA, TGY, and YEA. The sediment DNA was subjected to high-throughput Illumina sequencing, followed by quality control, assembly, and open read
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile microbial communities, antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence factors in sediments from three sites along the Yamuna River near Agra, India. The work reveals how anthropogenic pollution shapes the resistome and virulome in riverine sediments, highlighting sediments as reservoirs for clinically relevant AMR genes.

papers.title: LMDmapper: an open-source desktop tool for spatial mapping of laser microdissection samples.
papers.abstract: Laser microdissection (LMD) enables researchers to isolate targeted microsamples from microscopy slide specimens for downstream molecular analyses. While traditionally employed for isolating eukaryotic cells from complex tissues, LMD is starting to be used for micro-scale spatial microbiome analyses, which require the precise location of the microsamples to be tracked for downstream spatial analyses. To address this need, we present LMDmapper, an open-source desktop application that allows designing, tracking and logging micron-scale spatial microsample data and metadata from LMD sessions. The
papers.summary: LMDmapper is a new open-source desktop application that helps researchers design, track, and log micron-scale spatial coordinates and metadata for laser microdissection samples. It addresses the emerging need for precise spatial tracking in micro-scale spatial microbiome analyses, where sample location is critical for downstream spatial interpretation.

papers.title: Targeting cancer hallmarks with microbiome-derived bacteriocins and postbiotics: molecular mechanisms and translational opportunities in oncology.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome is an abundant reservoir of bioactive molecules with considerable therapeutic potential in oncology. Among these microbial products, bacteriocins and other postbiotic metabolites have emerged as promising anticancer agents due to their diverse biological activities and ability to modulate multiple cancer-related pathways. Growing evidence suggests that microbiome-derived compounds may provide novel opportunities for the development of safer and more targeted cancer therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review examines how bacteriocins and other postbiotic metabolites produced by the human microbiome can act as anticancer agents by modulating multiple cancer hallmark pathways. It discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects and outlines translational opportunities for developing safer, more targeted cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Sishen wan modulates gut microbial and short-chain fatty-acid imbalances and ameliorates behavioral and inflammatory abnormalities in mice with chronic sleep deprivation.
papers.abstract: Chronic sleep deprivation (CSD) disrupts mood-related behavior, gut microbial ecology, and inflammatory homeostasis. Sishen Wan (SSW), a medicinal plant formula used clinically for chronic diarrhea, has shown microbiota- and inflammation-modulating effects in colitis models, but its protective effects under sleep-deprivation conditions remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether Sishen Wan (SSW), a traditional Chinese medicinal formula, can counteract the negative effects of chronic sleep deprivation in mice. The authors find that SSW treatment rebalances gut microbial communities and short-chain fatty acid levels, and improves behavioral and inflammatory abnormalities caused by sleep loss. The work suggests a gut-microbiome-mediated mechanism for SSW's protective effects.

papers.title: The circulating metatranscriptome in acute myeloid leukemia patients: an RNA-seq reanalysis.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome comprises the collection of microbiota residing on or within human tissues. It is now well-established that microbial composition impacts an individual's health. In the cancer realm, the vast majority of microbiome studies have been focused either on the gut, or at the site of solid tumors. Few studies have assessed microbial content at the site of hematological malignancies - blood and bone marrow. Here we characterize the circulating metatranscriptome (i.e. the bacterial and viral RNA in circulation) of 411 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). We find that the cir
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed RNA-seq data from 411 acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients to characterize the circulating metatranscriptome—the bacterial and viral RNA present in blood. It represents one of the few efforts to profile microbial content in hematological malignancies rather than solid tumors or the gut, establishing a baseline for how microbial RNA in circulation relates to AML.

papers.title: Age-specific alterations in gut microbiota-plasma metabolome networks in first-episode, drug-naïve major depressive disorder: adolescent versus adult patients.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) exhibits pronounced age-related pathophysiological heterogeneity, yet the distinct signatures of the microbiota-gut-brain (MGB) axis between adolescent and adult patients remain inadequately characterized. This study aimed to elucidate age-specific MGB axis dysregulation by integrating gut microbiota profiling, plasma metabolomics, and their interactive networks in first-episode, drug-naïve MDD patients across these two developmental stages.
papers.summary: This study compares gut microbiota and plasma metabolome profiles, along with their interaction networks, between adolescent and adult patients experiencing their first episode of drug-naïve major depressive disorder. The authors identify age-specific patterns of microbiota-gut-brain axis dysregulation, suggesting that MDD pathophysiology differs between developmental stages. These findings highlight the need for age-tailored diagnostic and therapeutic approaches in depression.

papers.title: Sampling method influences hemolymph bacterial communities in the eastern oyster, Crassostrea virginica.
papers.abstract: As the microbiome becomes increasingly recognized for its role in driving animal health and disease, accurate characterization of microbial community composition is essential. With this research comes the critical need for standardized sampling methods along with an understanding of the biases inherent to these methods. In oysters, hemolymph is a valuable system for microbiome research due to its diverse physiological functions, role as an indicator of health, and ease of collection. Unfortunately, much of the current literature regarding oyster hemolymph microbiome composition is opaque in it
papers.summary: This study examines how different sampling methods affect the composition of bacterial communities detected in eastern oyster hemolymph. The authors find that the choice of sampling technique introduces biases in the microbial taxa recovered, highlighting the need for standardized protocols in oyster microbiome research. The work underscores that methodological transparency is essential for accurate characterization of hemolymph microbiomes.

papers.title: Microbiome-metabolome interaction reveals rhizosphere ecological, bioactive, and antioxidant responses of Paeonia lactiflora Pall. to intercropping and harvest timing.
papers.abstract: Paeonia lactiflora Pall. (P. lactiflora) is a medicinal plant with considerable economic value. During its growth, root secondary metabolism and rhizosphere microbes interact closely; however, no systematic study has examined microbiome and metabolome dynamics under different planting systems and harvest times. To address this, we employed amplicon sequencing for microbial diversity and untargeted metabolomics for metabolite profiling. The datasets were then integrated, and correlation analysis was performed. We measured paeoniflorin by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), total phen
papers.summary: This study integrated rhizosphere microbiome (amplicon sequencing) and metabolome (untargeted metabolomics) data from Paeonia lactiflora under different intercropping systems and harvest times, revealing how planting practices shape microbial communities and root secondary metabolites. The authors further linked these changes to ecological, bioactive, and antioxidant responses, including paeoniflorin content measured by HPLC. The work highlights microbiome-metabolome interactions as a potential lever for optimizing cultivation and harvest timing in medicinal plants.

papers.title: The effectiveness of the intervention model based on cognitive behavioral therapy in reducing risky sexual behaviors among MSM.
papers.abstract: Based on CBT theory and the Internet, we established an intervention model targeting high-risk sexual behavior patterns in MSM. We then conducted a randomized controlled trial (n = 50) to assess the impact of the CBT-based intervention on high-risk sexual behaviors and gut microbiota changes in this population.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial tested an internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) intervention designed to reduce risky sexual behaviors among men who have sex with men (MSM). The study also examined changes in gut microbiota as a secondary outcome, linking a behavioral intervention to microbiome shifts.

papers.title: Social and biological pathways linking relationships with companion animals to human well-being.
papers.abstract: Companion animals are widely recognized for their potential to support human mental health and well-being. These benefits may arise through changes in social relationships and physiological processes. This study examined whether dog and cat ownership and attachment promote closer social relationships and higher well-being, the relative magnitude of direct and indirect effects of companion animals on well-being, and whether physiological factors, including cortisol concentration and gut microbiota composition, are involved in these processes.
papers.summary: This study investigates how dog and cat ownership and attachment may improve human well-being through both social pathways (closer relationships) and biological pathways (cortisol levels and gut microbiota composition). It aims to quantify the relative direct and indirect effects of companion animals on well-being and test whether physiological factors mediate these benefits.

papers.title: Anaerobic stress index to predict microbial ecological shifts in clear aligners.
papers.abstract: Clear aligners are clinically perceived as periodontally 'friendlier' than fixed appliances (FA), yet localized gingivitis persists. Salivary diagnostics often mask site-specific dysbiosis through a 'dilution effect'. This study aimed to characterize distinct ecological pressures and propose a novel anaerobic stress index (ASI) to quantify localized microbial burden.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the distinct ecological pressures on oral microbial communities in patients wearing clear aligners versus fixed orthodontic appliances, arguing that salivary diagnostics mask site-specific dysbiosis. The authors propose a novel anaerobic stress index (ASI) to quantify localized microbial burden and predict ecological shifts.

papers.title: Current Concepts in Periprosthetic Joint Infection: Modern Biomarkers, Microbiome Insights, Molecular Diagnostics, and Emerging Prevention Strategies.
papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains one of the leading causes of revision arthroplasty and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Diagnosis remains challenging because of heterogeneous clinical presentations, the limited sensitivity of conventional inflammatory markers in chronic and low-grade infections, culture-negative cases, and biofilm-mediated pathogen persistence. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in the diagnosis and prevention of PJI, with a particular focus on synovial and serum biomarkers, microbiome-related susceptibility,
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent advances in diagnosing and preventing periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), a major complication of joint replacement surgery. It highlights modern synovial and serum biomarkers, molecular diagnostics that improve on conventional culture methods, microbiome-related susceptibility factors, and emerging prevention strategies. The focus is on overcoming challenges like culture-negative infections and biofilm persistence.

papers.title: The association between neonatal respiratory distress syndrome and gut microbiota dysbiosis: evidence from metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) is a common and life-threatening respiratory disorder that affects newborns, significantly impacting their health and survival rates. In recent years, the potential role of the gut-lung axis in NRDS has garnered increasing attention; however, the specific mechanisms involved remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between NRDS and gut microbial composition and functional profiles using shotgun metagenomic sequencing.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbial composition and functional profiles of newborns with neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (NRDS) against controls. The findings provide evidence of gut microbiota dysbiosis in NRDS, supporting a potential role for the gut-lung axis in this condition. However, the specific mechanisms linking microbial changes to NRDS remain to be clarified.

papers.title: Host identity dominates over intra-ruminal spatial variation in shaping the rumen microbiome of Holstein-Friesian dairy cows.
papers.abstract: The rumen is a structurally complex fermentation chamber with distinct physicochemical zones, resulting in intra-ruminal biogeography and raising the question whether microbial communities vary spatially within the rumen. We investigated the extent of intra-ruminal microbial variation by analyzing rumen fluid collected from six rumen cannulated Holstein-Friesian dairy cows. Rumen fluid samples were obtained in duplicate from three anatomical rumen regions: the cranial sac (Front), the front ventral sac (Middle), and the middle ventral sac (Back).and subjected to 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequenci
papers.summary: This study examined whether microbial communities differ across three anatomical regions within the rumen of six cannulated Holstein-Friesian dairy cows using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. They found that host identity (which cow the sample came from) explained far more of the microbial community variation than the intra-ruminal sampling location. This suggests that a single rumen fluid sample may adequately represent a cow's rumen microbiome for most purposes.

papers.title: A γ-polyglutamic acid-based artificial biofilm for field delivery of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens KNU-28: an uncontrolled multi-orchard demonstration on peach gummosis with exploratory bark fungal community profiling.
papers.abstract: Peach gummosis, caused primarily by Botryosphaeria dothidea sensu lato, is a destructive canker disease with few environmentally friendly management options. Here we report an uncontrolled pre/post field demonstration of a γ-polyglutamic acid-based artificial biofilm - a biodegradable delivery platform whose agent-agnostic design remains untested - encapsulating Bacillus amyloliquefaciens KNU-28 across 143 trees in 18 commercial peach orchards in South Korea. Severity declined from a pre-treatment mean of 4.12 (April) to 2.32 by August (76.2% of 143 trees improved by ≥1 point) and to 1.78 by O
papers.summary: This study tested a biodegradable γ-polyglutamic acid-based artificial biofilm encapsulating Bacillus amyloliquefaciens KNU-28 for controlling peach gummosis across 143 trees in 18 commercial orchards in South Korea. Disease severity dropped from a pre-treatment mean of 4.12 in April to 2.32 by August, with 76.2% of trees improving by at least one point, and exploratory bark fungal community profiling was also performed. The demonstration was uncontrolled (no untreated comparison group), so efficacy cannot be definitively attributed to the treatment.
